description: Canonical Cognix GTM hard-test scenarios. These fixtures use explicit signal surfaces to test the diagnostic/scoring engine directly, independent of intake parser behavior.

scenarios.name: Strong RevOps pipeline trust launch
scenarios.assumption: Structured signal surfaces are used so this validates scoring calibration directly, not Sorting Hat parsing.

signals.launch-message: NovaOps AI helps RevOps leaders stop walking into pipeline reviews with numbers nobody trusts before quarter-end executive pipeline reviews.
signals.target-buyer: RevOps leaders at B2B SaaS companies.
signals.buyer-pain: RevOps leaders struggle with broken pipeline reviews when Salesforce, Gong, Clari, and spreadsheets tell different stories before executive meetings.
signals.value-prop: NovaOps AI helps RevOps leaders protect forecast confidence and pipeline trust before quarter-end executive pipeline reviews.
signals.campaign-copy: Stop walking into pipeline reviews with numbers nobody trusts.
signals.sales-talk-track: Sales lead with pipeline trust, forecast confidence, and the cost of walking into executive reviews with conflicting numbers before quarter-end.
signals.objections: If buyers ask whether this is another dashboard, reps explain that NovaOps AI is not another dashboard because it reconciles the pipeline trust gap across systems.
signals.competitive-framing: Not another dashboard. NovaOps AI is a pipeline trust layer for executive revenue reviews.
signals.customer-proof: Reduced weekly pipeline prep from 6 hours to 90 minutes.
signals.launch-goal: Convert RevOps demo requests by protecting forecast confidence before executive pipeline reviews.

scenarios.name: Generic AI launch intelligence with commercial risk
scenarios.assumption: Matches the SignalForge commercial-risk hard test from the product QA discussion.

signals.launch-message: SignalForge is built to find the launch story that will break before campaign budget goes live.
signals.target-buyer: CMOs and VP Marketing leaders at Series B to Series D SaaS companies.
signals.buyer-pain: CMOs risk spending budget on a launch story that does not convert into qualified demos.
signals.value-prop: SignalForge helps CMOs detect launch-to-pipeline risk before campaign spend goes live.
signals.campaign-copy: AI-powered launch intelligence for modern product marketing teams.
signals.sales-talk-track: Sales should lead with launch-to-pipeline risk and ask whether the current story will create qualified demo intent.
signals.objections: CMOs worry the launch will create activity but miss the 40 qualified demo target.
signals.customer-proof: Pilot teams used SignalForge to catch buyer-facing dilution before paid spend launched.
signals.launch-goal: $97,000 launch investment; 40 qualified demo target; $60,000 to $120,000 ARR influence at risk.

expected.dominantFracture: Generic AI positioning weakens CMO-level demo intent

scenarios.name: Good internal strategy, weak buyer-facing page
scenarios.assumption: The calibrated fixture keeps only the explicit strategic baseline, public page, value proposition, and CTA surfaces. Adding fuller buyer/proof/sales surfaces currently lifts the risk tier to Medium, so those belong in a separate synthesis fixture rather than this scoring guard.

signals.launch-message: Internal launch strategy: ComplianceOps prevents delayed SOC 2 audits by finding last-minute evidence gaps and control gaps before formal review.
signals.value-prop: ComplianceOps gives teams pre-audit intelligence so they can fix evidence gaps before audit readiness is at risk.
signals.campaign-copy: Modern compliance intelligence for fast-moving security teams.

expected.dominantFracture: Public-facing message does not carry the internal strategy

scenarios.name: Awareness-heavy launch with weak conversion path
scenarios.assumption: Fixture preserves the awareness/activity goal, broad buyer, weak pain, missing proof, and passive CTA needed to trigger the high-risk conversion-path guardrail.

signals.launch-message: FlowPilot is a flexible AI workspace for operations teams, GTM leaders, and finance leaders.
signals.target-buyer: Operations leaders, GTM leaders, finance leaders, and business teams.
signals.buyer-pain: Teams do too much manual work across disconnected processes.
signals.value-prop: FlowPilot helps every team move faster with intelligent workflow automation.
signals.campaign-copy: Unlock productivity with intelligent automation for every team.
signals.sales-talk-track: Sales is unsure which pain to lead with because there are many use cases across sales, marketing, operations, and finance.
signals.objections: Prospects may ask why they need another workflow tool.
signals.launch-goal: $78,000 launch budget; drive impressions, traffic, page visits, and demo requests from awareness campaigns.

expected.dominantFracture: Launch motion creates activity but not qualified demo intent

scenarios.name: Narrow ICP, strong pain, weak proof
scenarios.assumption: Preserves specific VP CS renewal/churn/adoption language and intentionally keeps proof unquantified.

signals.launch-message: RetainIQ helps VP CS teams find renewal risk before it becomes churn risk.
signals.target-buyer: VP CS at B2B SaaS companies with enterprise renewal books.
signals.buyer-pain: Customer adoption has already dropped before executive sponsors surface renewal risk, putting expansion revenue and renewal conversations at risk.
signals.value-prop: RetainIQ identifies account risk signals before renewal conversations become late-stage churn escalations.
signals.campaign-copy: Find renewal risk before it turns into churn risk.
signals.sales-talk-track: Lead with dropped adoption, executive sponsor silence, renewal risk, and expansion revenue risk.
signals.objections: Buyers ask whether CS teams can trust early adoption risk signals; sales explains the account-risk workflow.
signals.competitive-framing: Not a CS platform replacement. RetainIQ flags account risk before renewal risk escalates.
signals.customer-proof: Three founding users validated the workflow, but quantified renewal impact is not available yet.
signals.launch-goal: Convert VP CS demo requests from accounts facing renewal and churn risk.

expected.dominantFracture: Proof gap may weaken late-stage demo conversion

scenarios.name: ICP-message mismatch
scenarios.assumption: CTA is intentionally not passive so the dominant fracture remains buyer/message mismatch rather than passive CTA.

signals.launch-message: SpendSync should help finance leaders detect spend leakage, budget leakage, and approval visibility risk before departmental forecasts drift.
signals.buyer-pain: CFOs need financial control, margin protection, forecast accuracy, spend leakage detection, and approval visibility.
signals.value-prop: SpendSync gives finance teams spend visibility before budget leakage damages forecast confidence.
signals.campaign-copy: Work smarter across every team with an intelligent workspace for productivity and cross-functional workflows.
signals.sales-talk-track: Sales is likely to describe team productivity and workflow automation.
signals.objections: CFOs may ask how this protects margin, forecast accuracy, spend leakage, and approval control.
signals.competitive-framing: Competitors lead with financial control and spend leakage.
signals.customer-proof: Early finance users found $240,000 in budget leakage in approval workflows.
signals.launch-goal: Convert CFO demo requests tied to spend leakage and forecast accuracy.

expected.dominantFracture: Target buyer and message are misaligned

scenarios.name: Strong proof, unclear CTA and conversion path
scenarios.assumption: Includes qualified demos/demo requests in the goal so the calibrated strong-proof weak-conversion-path guardrail triggers rather than a generic passive CTA result.

signals.launch-message: InvoiceIQ helps AP leaders find invoice exceptions before they become backlog.
signals.target-buyer: AP directors and finance operations leaders.
signals.buyer-pain: Invoice exceptions slow down AP teams and create backlog risk before month-end close.
signals.value-prop: InvoiceIQ identifies exception leakage and prioritizes AP work before unresolved invoices become operational backlog.
signals.sales-talk-track: Lead with invoice exception leakage, AP backlog, and operational drag before talking about workflow automation.
signals.objections: Buyers ask whether existing AP workflow tools already catch exceptions early enough.
signals.competitive-framing: Not generic AP automation. InvoiceIQ focuses on exception leakage and backlog prevention.
signals.customer-proof: Reduced invoice exception resolution time by 52%, cut backlog by 38%, and saved 420 AP hours in one quarter.
signals.launch-goal: Convert qualified demos and demo requests from finance operations buyers actively trying to reduce AP backlog risk.

expected.dominantFracture: Proof is strong but CTA and conversion path are weak
